title: Millwork Pre-Fabrication Review Checklist
subtitle: Track drawing changes, supporting decisions, field information, and open questions.
scope: Educational coordination aid. This is Groundstate’s suggested coordination checklist, not an official AWI document, compliance certification, or fabrication authorization. Use it alongside the project requirements and your shop’s established procedures.
before: Identify the package, issue date, affected scope, reviewer, and review date. Gather the returned shop drawings, review comments, relevant change records, supplier information, field records, and applicable release procedure.
reviewedMeaning: “Reviewed” means the comparison was made and recorded. It does not mean the item is approved or ready to fabricate.

sections.title: Current drawings and revisions
checks: Can you identify the exact drawing and package revisions being reviewed?
Have you compared the current detail with the relevant returned drawings and documented changes, including changes not clearly marked?
Do the affected production details, schedules, cut sheets, and shop packets agree with each other?
sections.note: Record the affected sheets and items. Do not assume the newest document establishes approval.

sections.title: Architect comments and submittal responses
checks: Which returned review applies to this item, and what does it cover?
Have applicable comments been incorporated or given a documented disposition?
Are changed details or substitutions supported by the required review, rather than merely appearing in a later drawing?
sections.note: Record the response, date, scope, and source location.

sections.title: RFIs, ASIs, and other changes
checks: Have you checked relevant RFI responses, Architect’s Supplemental Instructions, change orders, sketches, and correspondence for effects on this scope?
Can you trace each applicable instruction into the affected production information?
Where instructions conflict, or their status is unclear, is the question assigned for resolution through the project’s procedure?
sections.note: Record what changed and where. A discussion, instruction, and approval may serve different purposes.

sections.title: Supplier requirements and product cut sheets
checks: Does the product information match the model, components, and configuration currently scheduled?
Have you checked the affected dimensions and interfaces against the applicable supplier requirements—for example, cutouts, clearances, access, or removal space?
Does any supplier decision cover this exact configuration, including its stated limits?
sections.note: Record calculations and their inputs. Do not extend a configuration-specific acceptance to a changed detail without checking its scope.

sections.title: Field measurements and site conditions
checks: Are the relevant field records identifiable by location, date, units, and measurement reference?
Are finished dimensions distinguished from rough openings, substrates, carriers, and assumed finish buildups?
Are unverified dimensions, agreed hold dimensions, and unresolved site conditions identified for follow-up?
sections.note: Identify who needs to verify or coordinate the condition under the project’s arrangements.

sections.title: Applicable production-release requirements
checks: What review or release procedure applies to this item or portion of the package?
Are its required decisions, records, and authorizations present, with their scope and conditions understood?
Have remaining restrictions been communicated to the people preparing or receiving production information?
sections.note: Use the project’s actual procedure. Do not assume every project requires a separate written PM release.

sections.title: Conflicts, missing evidence, and follow-up
checks: Have you recorded demonstrated conflicts separately from missing information and unresolved decisions?
Does each open issue identify the affected item, supporting records, responsible person, and next action?
When an issue is resolved, will the affected production information be updated and the resolution communicated?
sections.note: A missing record does not prove that approval never occurred. An unresolved solution does not erase a demonstrated conflict.

finish: List the checks completed and issues still open. Refer unresolved items to the appropriate person through the established project process.
completionWarning: Completing this checklist does not establish engineering adequacy, field fit, standards compliance, or permission to fabricate.
methodQualification: The detailed prompts—especially record comparisons, supplier-scope checks, and issue tracking—are our proposed review method. They are not represented as verbatim AWI requirements.
howTo: Identify the package and scope you are reviewing.
Gather the relevant returned drawings, responses, changes, supplier information, and field records.
Work through the seven checks. Record references instead of relying on a tick alone.
Use an item-review sheet for each discrepancy or open question.
Route follow-up through the project’s established process, then record the resolution and affected document updates.

worksheet.title: Pre-Fabrication Item Review
worksheet.subtitle: Educational coordination record — not a fabrication release
worksheet.calculation: Comparison or calculation, including units and measurement basis
statuses: No discrepancy identified in this specific comparison
worksheet.finding: Finding — what do the available records establish?
worksheet.openQuestion: Open question — what is not established?
followUp: Applicable restriction or release requirement, with source
worksheet.blankWarning: Blank fields are not evidence of approval or completed review. These status labels describe the comparison only.
worksheet.responsibilityWarning: “Responsible person” means the person assigned to coordinate the next action; it does not transfer design, contractual, or release authority.

example.title: Completed WC27 worksheet example
example.fictional: Fictional training example. All project records, organizations, products, and people are invented. Suggested follow-up below is identified explicitly.
rows: Fictional North Annex, Level 2 east corridor; WC-27 cladding / SA-27 service-access cassette
Six supplied records, R01–R06. No review event or reviewer identity is invented.
SA-27 frame-mounting cutout and clear service passage
704 × 900 mm cutout; SJ-16 jambs consuming 16 mm each side; head and sill consuming 30 mm each. R06, p. 1, §2

Conflict demonstrated, plus decision/verification outstanding and release evidence not supplied
The scheduled current configuration does not meet the clear-width minimum. Referencing TD-27-09 does not establish supplier acceptance of the changed cutout.
What final configuration will satisfy the requirements and receive the applicable reviews? Revised architectural joint-layout review remains pending. R05 §1; R06 §3

Survey: 1295 mm from carrier C0 to the opposite finished wall. Working-depth requirement: 1260 mm from finished cladding face. Projection P remains unresolved. Depth = 1295 − P; P ≤ 35 mm is a derived limit, not an approved projection or confirmed fit. The 738 × 920 mm carrier opening is a different opening. R02 §3; R03 §§1–3; R06 §3
Suggested coordinator: project PM Noel Ash, with detailing and the applicable supplier/design reviewers. This worksheet does not invent a new assignment or recorded action.

Suggested: refer the width conflict for coordinated resolution; obtain applicable supplier and architectural reviews; establish P and verify working space; update affected production information. No corrective dimensions are prescribed.
R05 permits flitch matching and reservation of uncut stock only. CNC cutting and cassette assembly remain on hold pending interface resolution and written PM release. R01 §3; R05 §2
Coordinated cutting basis and signed release required by September 11, 16:00 to retain the September 14, 09:00 CNC slot. R05 §3. No outcome after the September 11, 13:00 package is supplied.
Not established. R06 states the release is not attached and describes its issue as a detailing transmittal. No subsequent release or completed notification is supplied. R06 §3
example.note: This single item review deliberately records different statuses for different questions. The width conflict is known; working depth, final design disposition, and release remain separate matters.

guidance.label: AWI 100, §3.2 — Manufacturer / supplier responsibility
guidance.text: Supports distinguishing displayed changes from requested approval, identifying applicable submittals, and checking returned review dispositions. The checklist is a selective suggested workflow, not a restatement of the standard.

guidance.label: AWI 100, §§3.3 and 3.4(g) — Field and design changes
guidance.text: Addresses hold dimensions and communication of design/field changes, including responsibility dependent on contractual relationships.

guidance.label: Practitioner context — WOODWEB, 2010
guidance.text: A discussion of measurement forms, cross-checking, and information retrieval informed usability choices. Its performance assertions are not adopted.
